additions.reason: The Torah's entire theme is resurrection. The text explicitly says: 'וּמִמֶּנּוּ יִתְחַדֵּשׁ בִּנְיַן הַגּוּף בִּשְׁעַת תְּחִיַּת הַמֵּתִים' — from the Luz bone the body will be rebuilt at the time of resurrection. The עֶצֶם לוּז is defined as the bone from which תְּחִיַּת הַמֵּתִים emerges. This is a bechina relationship: the Luz bone IS the resurrection-seed, i.e., the same essential reality viewed from two angles. It belongs in Package 2 alongside עֶצֶם לוּז and עִקַּר נֶחָמוֹתֵינוּ.

additions.reason: The text describes Leah as 'נֻקְבָּא רִאשׁוֹנָה' — the first feminine principle — specifically in the context of her being 'in the nape (ערף).' This phrase is used as the defining characterization of Leah's role in the ערף dimension. It is a bechina of לאה and of the entire ערף cluster — the nape-zone as the first/hidden feminine level that must be traversed before reaching Rachel. Belongs in Package 1.
additions.source_quote: הֵם רוֹמְזִים לִבְחִינַת לֵאָה שֶׁהִיא בָּעֹרֶף, שֶׁהִיא נֻקְבָּא רִאשׁוֹנָה

additions.reason: The text states 'עֹרֶף גִּימַטְרִיָּא ש"נ רָאשֵׁי תֵבוֹת: שַׁבַּת נַחֲמוּ' — the gematria of ערף is ש"נ (350), whose roshei teivot (acronym) spell שַׁבַּת נַחֲמוּ. The dataset records שבת נחמו — ערף as a bechina edge, but the intermediary ש"נ (as the numeric/gematria bridge) is itself the conceptual link. It could stand as its own node in Package 1, though it may be considered an alias of ערף / שבת נחמו rather than a distinct concept.

analysis_notes.good_evil_mirror: This Torah has no explicit evil mirror. It is entirely focused on consolation and resurrection. The mourning period (Three Weeks, Tisha B'Av) represents the destruction/exile dimension, but no bechina edges represent evil-polarity concepts. The 'evil' background is the destruction of the Temple and the exile of the Shekhinah, but these are not encoded in bechina edges for this Torah.
analysis_notes.note_on_package_1_polarity: Package 1 is classified as neutral because the concepts — nape, Luz bone's location, gematria connections, Leah as 'first feminine' — are structural/anatomical objects used as metaphors. Leah herself has positive connotations here (she is the gateway to the holy) but the package as a whole functions as a neutral structural cluster. The positive teaching belongs to Package 2.
